transcript.answer:
Short answer
- The cache pod is saturated (max connections reached) and queuing connections; that causes checkout-api calls to the cache to time out. Root cause: a single cache instance (one Endpoint) hitting its max_active connection limit (40) under client load from multiple producers (report-worker, inventory-sync, checkout-api).

Evidence (what I inspected)
- Pods (namespace shop)
  - checkout-api: checkout-api-58f9d6b876-lckwq (10.244.3.4) and checkout-api-58f9d6b876-xztgj (10.244.1.3) — both Running, Ready.
  - cache pod: cache-9ffcf47fc-5d4xf (10.244.3.2) — Running, Ready.
- Service
  - Service "cache" (ClusterIP 10.96.204.9) -> port 6379; Endpoints / EndpointSlice contains only the single cache pod 10.244.3.2 (i.e. only one replica behind the service).
- checkout-api logs (last 1 hour; filtered for errors/timeouts)
  - Repeated entries like:
    2026-10-07T09:05:11Z ERROR checkout-api cache GET cart:9366 timed out after 2.0s (cache:6379) [TimeoutError]
  - Many TimeoutError messages between ~09:05 and ~09:08 UTC. (Query: last 1 hour; matched ~110 logs.)
- cache pod logs (last 1 hour)
  - Startup line: cache-server starting log_level=debug max_active=40
  - Repeated connection-table entries showing saturation:
    2026-10-07T09:05:08Z conn-table active=40/40 queued=3 peers=10.244.1.4:5,10.244.3.5:5,...
    2026-10-07T09:06:08Z conn-table active=40/40 queued=27 peers=10.244.1.4:13,10.244.3.5:13,10.244.1.5:11,10.244.3.4:2,10.244.1.3:2,10.244.3.3:1
  - These logs show max_active=40, active connections at 40 and a non-zero queued count (up to 27) while many client IPs are connected → connection saturation and queueing.
- NetworkPolicy
  - A NetworkPolicy named cache-ingress exists and allows ingress to cache:6379 from pods with label tier=backend.
  - checkout-api pods have label tier=backend — therefore network policy is permitting the traffic, not blocking it.

Why this causes checkout-api timeouts
- checkout-api times out waiting for replies from cache:6379 (client-side timeout 2.0s).
- The cache is single-instance and its connection capacity (max_active=40) is exhausted by traffic from multiple services (report-worker replicas, inventory-sync, checkout-api). New client requests are queued by the cache and not serviced within checkout-api's 2s timeout, causing the TimeoutError seen in checkout-api logs.

Root cause (concise)
- Single cache pod + low max_active (40) + concurrent load from multiple producers → cache connection saturation → requests queue and exceed checkout-api's 2s client timeout.

Remediation — immediate and medium-term (concrete commands you can run)
1) Immediate mitigation (fastest):
   - Scale cache to more replicas (if the cache implementation supports multiple stateless replicas behind a ClusterIP):
     kubectl get deployment cache -n shop
     kubectl scale deployment cache --replicas=3 -n shop
   - If cache is stateful and cannot be simply replicated, temporarily raise its allowed connections (max_active) or increase resources/config so it can handle more concurrent connections:
     kubectl edit deployment cache -n shop
     (edit args/env/configmap to increase max_active to a higher value, e.g. 200; exact key depends on your chart/config.)
   - Note: scaling or changing max_active may require corresponding configuration changes in the cache configmap or deployment args; inspect the deployment before editing:
     kubectl get deploy cache -n shop -o yaml

2) Short-to-medium term (recommended):
   - Deploy a proper clustered cache (Redis cluster, sentinel, or managed Redis) or use a StatefulSet with sharding so the service has multiple endpoints that share load.
   - Add readiness checks and horizontalPodAutoscaler for the cache (if stateless) or autoscale front-end clients to reduce burst load.
   - Add connection-limits / pooling throttles on high-throughput producers (report-worker) to avoid many concurrent connections. From the logs, report-worker pods (10.244.1.4, 10.244.3.5, 10.244.1.5) are heavy peers; reduce their client connection concurrency.

3) App-side fixes:
   - Increase checkout-api cache client timeout temporarily if acceptable (avoids immediate 2s failures while you fix the cache capacity).
   - Ensure checkout-api and other clients reuse connections (connection pooling) and set conservative pool sizes. (checkout-api env shows POOL_SIZE=2, POOL_RECYCLE_SECONDS=15 — but other services appear to open many connections.)

4) Observability + prevention:
   - Add metrics and alerting on cache: active connections, queued connections, connection errors; alert when active == max_active or queued > 0.
   - Add capacity tests / load shedding for producers (circuit breaker) so a single service doesn't overload the cache.
   - Add an SLO/limit: limit per-pod connection count at the client side if cache cannot scale horizontally.

How I mapped the evidence to the cause (short trace)
- checkout-api log: consistent TimeoutError to cache:6379.
- cache log: "max_active=40" + "active=40/40 queued=..." + peers listing including checkout-api and report-worker pod IPs.
- Endpoint list: only one cache pod behind the "cache" service.
- NetworkPolicy: allows backend pods, so not blocking.

If you want, I can:
- Scale the cache deployment to 3 replicas for you (runs kubectl scale).
- Inspect the cache Deployment/ConfigMap to show where to change max_active and provide a patch.
- Show which client pods are contributing the most connections (map IP → pod name + per-pod connection counts from cache logs).
Tell me which action you want me to run next (I can apply non-destructive read-only checks immediately; scaling/edits require your approval).
